transcription_method: Manual transcription from supplied DOCX/PDF text. Light spelling, punctuation and whitespace normalization only. Where the source presents a multi-part ILO as one statement, its related components remain grouped; topic headings and assessment methods are not relabelled as ILOs.
scope_note: Granular transcription of the knowledge and psychomotor ILO statements for Neurology, Psychiatry, Rheumatology, Dermatology and Andrology from printed pages 4–16. Topic lists and end-of-module assessment descriptions are excluded as ILOs.

outcomes.transcribed_text: Describe hemiplegia, cerebrovascular stroke, transient ischaemic attack, convulsions and epilepsy, Parkinson’s disease, multiple sclerosis, motor-neuron diseases, myopathy, myasthenia, involuntary movements, movement disorders and ataxia in terms of definition, classification, causes, pathogenesis, clinical picture and outline management.

Identify diagnostic approaches for coma, confusion and delirium; peripheral neuropathies and ascending paralysis (Guillain–Barré syndrome); spinal-cord compression and acute paraplegia; raised intracranial tension and subarachnoid haemorrhage; and cerebral venous sinus thrombosis.
Describe causes, diagnostic approach and clinical picture of headache.
Outline a diagnostic approach to low-back pain.
Formulate a differential diagnosis for paraplegia and low-back pain.
Describe mental and psychiatric status assessment.
Mention psychiatric emergencies and outline a plan of management for psychiatric emergencies.
Identify high-risk groups (women, children and older people) for psychiatric illness.
Define psychoses and personality disorders.
Describe substance abuse, liaison psychiatry and suicide.

Explain mood disorders, adjustment disorders, somatoform disorders, anxiety disorders, schizophrenia and organic mental disorders in terms of pathogenesis, clinical presentation and lines of management.
Formulate therapeutic approaches in psychiatric patients.
Describe types, pathogenesis, clinical picture and outcomes of rheumatoid arthritis, lupus erythematosus, osteoporosis, osteoarthritis and low-back pain.
Outline a diagnostic approach to mechanical and inflammatory back pain and to a patient with monoarthritis or polyarthritis.

Identify diagnostic approaches to vasculitis (classification), systemic sclerosis/scleroderma, Sjögren syndrome, seronegative rheumatic diseases (ankylosing spondylitis and reactive arthritis), crystal-induced arthropathies (gout and pseudogout), soft-tissue rheumatism (fibromyalgia, dermatomyositis and polymyositis), and metabolic/nutritional bone disease (osteoporosis, osteomalacia and rickets).
Mention basic principles of rehabilitation of rheumatologic and neurological diseases.
Outline management plans for rheumatoid arthritis, lupus erythematosus, osteoporosis, osteoarthritis and low-back pain.
Describe mechanisms of action, indications, contraindications and adverse effects of conventional synthetic and biological disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, NSAIDs and corticosteroids.
Take a focused history of illness from a patient with dermatological complaints.
Demonstrate proper use of medical instruments.
Outline and interpret physical and microscopic parameters of semen analysis.

Recognize indications of dermatological diagnostic and therapeutic tools, including Wood’s light, skin biopsy, cryotherapy, electrocautery, intralesional injections, phototherapy and potassium-hydroxide examination.
List causes of bacterial skin infections and describe different skin lesions.
Discuss aetiology, clinical picture and diagnosis of molluscum contagiosum, human papillomavirus infection, herpes simplex infection (non-genital and genital), varicella and herpes zoster.
Discuss aetiology, clinical picture and diagnosis of dermatophyte infections at different sites, pityriasis versicolor and cutaneous, oropharyngeal, genital and nail candidiasis.
Discuss aetiology, pathogenesis, manifestations and diagnosis of leprosy.
Discuss aetiology, clinical features and diagnosis of erythrasma, impetigo, ecthyma, furuncles, carbuncles, erysipelas and cellulitis.
Describe cutaneous reactions to arthropod bites and discuss manifestations and diagnosis of pediculosis and scabies.
Explain pathogenesis of psoriasis vulgaris, pityriasis rosea and lichen planus.
Describe diagnosis and clinical picture of psoriasis vulgaris, pityriasis rubra pilaris, pityriasis rosea and lichen planus.
List different types of eczema.
Explain pathogenesis, clinical picture and diagnosis of atopic dermatitis, seborrhoeic dermatitis and irritant and allergic contact dermatitis.
Explain aetiology, pathogenesis, clinical picture and diagnosis of acute and chronic urticaria, angioedema and anaphylaxis.

Describe aetiology, clinical picture and diagnosis of erythema multiforme, Stevens–Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, exanthematous drug reactions, drug-induced acute urticaria/angioedema and fixed drug eruption.
Explain aetiology, pathogenesis, types and diagnosis of vitiligo.
Describe pathogenesis, clinical picture and diagnosis of squamous-cell carcinoma, basal-cell carcinoma, alopecia areata, telogen effluvium and pattern hair loss.
Discuss clinical picture and diagnosis of acne vulgaris and acne variants; describe the clinical picture of discoid lupus erythematosus and erythema nodosum.
Describe skin manifestations of liver disease, kidney disease and diabetes mellitus.
Describe aetiology, clinical presentation and diagnosis of bacterial, viral, fungal and other genital ulcers; discuss non-STD genital ulcers and their differential diagnosis.
Describe aetiology, incubation period, transmission, clinical pictures in males and females, complications, differential diagnosis, management and follow-up of gonococcal urethritis.
Discuss aetiology, differential diagnosis and laboratory investigations of trichomoniasis, chlamydiasis and candidiasis.
Discuss aetiology, pathogenesis, clinical picture and differential diagnosis of syphilis.
Differentiate infertility, sterility and subfertility and describe the aetiological factors of male infertility.
Discuss the diagnostic approach to male infertility.
Describe the definition, epidemiology and diagnostic tests of erectile dysfunction.
Discuss management of molluscum contagiosum, human papillomavirus infection, herpes simplex infection (non-genital and genital), varicella and herpes zoster.
Discuss management of dermatophyte infections, pityriasis versicolor and cutaneous, oropharyngeal, genital and nail candidiasis.
Discuss management of leprosy, erythrasma, impetigo, ecthyma, furuncles, carbuncles, erysipelas, cellulitis, pediculosis and scabies.
Outline management of psoriasis vulgaris, pityriasis rubra pilaris, pityriasis rosea and lichen planus.
Explain management of atopic, seborrhoeic, irritant contact and allergic contact dermatitis.
Explain management of acute and chronic urticaria, angioedema, anaphylaxis, erythema multiforme, Stevens–Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis and drug eruptions.
Discuss management modalities for vitiligo, squamous-cell carcinoma, basal-cell carcinoma, alopecia areata, telogen effluvium, pattern hair loss, acne vulgaris and acne variants.
Discuss management of trichomoniasis, chlamydiasis, candidiasis and syphilis; outline medical and surgical treatment of male infertility and enumerate treatments for erectile dysfunction.
Identify therapeutic uses and adverse effects of dapsone, isotretinoin, systemic antifungals and topical corticosteroids, antifungals, antibiotics, antiscabitics and calcineurin inhibitors.

Take a complete neurological history, elicit presenting problems and relevant details, past medical/surgical, family and social history, medications and allergies, perform an appropriate review of systems, and establish rapport.

Perform general and focused neurological examination in logical sequence; show sensitivity and respect, explain procedures, and use medical instruments including stethoscope, sphygmomanometer, reflex hammer and tuning fork.

Use appropriate draping, maintain dignity and privacy, demonstrate empathy and professional conduct, communicate findings concisely using accepted terminology, and present positive and negative findings systematically.
Use simple diagnostic procedures available in district hospitals to reach a diagnosis and diagnose medical diseases prevalent in the community.
Take a psychiatric history, elicit presenting problems, relevant past medical, family and social history and medications, perform a relevant review of systems, and establish rapport.
Perform general clinical examination and focused mental-status examination in logical sequence.
Show sensitivity and respect, explain examination procedures, maintain dignity and privacy, and demonstrate empathy and ethical conduct with patients and families.
Communicate psychiatric history and examination findings in accepted medical terminology and present significant positive and negative findings systematically.
Diagnose psychiatric diseases prevalent in the community and make recommendations for further investigation, management or referral.
Negotiate with the patient and family, considering cultural and religious beliefs, to arrive at an acceptable action plan.
Take and record a full and organized rheumatological history.
Perform physical assessment of the musculoskeletal system and special clinical tests relevant to the provisional diagnosis of each rheumatic disease.
Design a management strategy proportional to the rheumatological diagnosis.
Take a complete dermatological history, examine a dermatology patient, recognize primary and secondary skin lesions, and use essential diagnostic tools in the dermatology clinic.
Read and interpret selected dermatological and andrological investigations and recognize topical and systemic drugs used in dermatology.
Demonstrate familiarity with dermatological therapeutic modalities including PUVA, narrow-band UVB, intralesional injections, electrocautery and cryotherapy.
